ratings_why.fun: Reading order, slot gaps and the back-row wrong-way mode give real choices each turn; a few cards (Hobby Lantern, Tiddy Mun, Irrlicht) are one-job filler.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because the enemy's own keywords become your weapon (an Astray Cleave hits three of its own units) and empty slots are the resource, which no current tribe or generic auto-battler tribe does.

verdict_why: The Marsh Light's rules don't work as written with Drowned and 'Astray at most once', and the self-hit line depends on that ruling.

points.text: Marsh Light goes out before damage, so it's unclear whether it is Drowned when your own Astray attack hits it; the Hoard-Keeper and Aarnivalkea self-hit line relies on it. Say whether going out to an ally's hit counts as Drowned.
An already-Astray attack that hits a Flit unit or a Marsh Light can't go Astray again. Say what happens: does it land, is it lost, or does the Light still go out?
Hobby Lantern is plain Flit. A small cross-hook, such as leaving a Marsh Light behind only when Follette or Spunkie is on board, would give the T1 a reason to stay late.
Tiddy Mun only counts enemy units. Letting it also count your empty slots would tie it into the fen and create a fill-or-leave choice.
Add one controlled self-hit card (aim an ally at your chosen Marsh Light) so the Drowned build has a reliable engine, not just Phos's random back-row mode.

standouts.why: Gaffer Turncoat turns a Mire wall into a 12-Attack glass cannon that Fingerpost then aims at its own side; also kills 0-Attack Eggs and walls.
Fresh-Ink Mapseller makes your gaps aim: you read the next board and leave the slot across their Cleave or Bristle unit empty.
Jack o' the Turnip is symmetric, so it is both the Drowning multiplier and a way to crack your own Ooze open early.

weakest.why: Hobby Lantern is a vanilla dodge with no link to the other cards beyond Follette.
Tiddy Mun is more Astray sources with no decision attached.
Irrlicht mostly repeats Flit plus Marsh Light already on other cards.

flags.note: Old Will with Jack and Aarnivalkea can wipe a full enemy board in one wave and pay +1/+1 per Drowning; check golden Old Will.
Aarnivalkea has no per-fight cap and counts both sides, so Moon's many Marsh Lights plus self-hits could stack fast.
Whether a Marsh Light hit by its own side is Drowned, and what an already-Astray attack does to it.
